papers.title: Spectral Regimes of Truncated sinc-Power and Pulse-Train Kernels: Edge Exponents, Per-Edge Plunges, and the Landau-Widom Limit
papers.summary: A signal band-limited to one rectangular band and observed through a finite window is the classical concentration problem of Slepian, Landau, Pollak, and Widom. The eigenvalues of the operator cluster near one and near zero, separated by a transition called the plunge. The plunge width grows like the logarithm of the window length, with a universal coefficient of one over pi squared set by the band-edge jump. This paper follows the clusters and the plunge as the band is deformed. An elementwise power of the kernel smooths the band edge, and the plunge gives way to a power-law edge with exponent one less than the power. Disjoint copies of the band widen the plunge in proportion to the number of band edges, as the multiple-interval theorem of Landau and Widom implies, so the coefficient is a per-edge constant. Shrinking each band to a line gives the classical finite-rank operator. Overlapping bands give a multilevel staircase, and a self-similar band gives a cluster hierarchy governed by the Cantor dimension. At the smooth edge, rescaled eigenvalues do not collapse onto one curve. The edge descriptor passes from a constant to an exponent to an integer to a fractal dimension. For the single band, classical results place all eigenfilter zeros on the unit circle, with more of them inside the band as the order rises, so the dominant eigenvectors act as lowpass filters.

papers.title: Core-Lock Scheduling for 5G NR LDPC Decoders
papers.summary: Accelerating iterative LDPC decoding while preserving error-correction reliability is a critical challenge in latency-constrained 5G New Radio (NR) and non-terrestrial networks. This paper proposes a hardware-efficient core-lock scheduling mechanism that evaluates the core syndrome weight after each layer update to selectively bypass extension layers. With the selected threshold $θ{=}0.20$, the mechanism reduces decoding latency by up to 31.3\% when integrated with static schedules, and by up to 45.5\% compared to alternative dynamic schemes utilizing the full parity-check matrix, without block error rate (BLER) degradation. Compared with an estimated fully parallel full-matrix checker, the core-only approach yields a 76\% reduction in shifter network area and a 73\% reduction in XOR gate count. For decoders with existing early termination, the proposed mechanism requires only a compact adder tree and a comparator.
papers.comment: 4 pages, 4 figures, 1 table. Accepted for publication in the 2026 IEEE 33rd International Conference on Electronics, Circuits and Systems (ICECS 2026). \c{opyright} 2026 IEEE

papers.title: 4D Point Splatting for mmWave Radar Micro-Doppler Differentiable Rendering
papers.summary: Millimeter-wave radar resolves the micrometer displacements of a moving body as micro-Doppler, enabling gait, gesture, activity, pose and vital-sign sensing. Each task relies on a downstream model trained on real data, yet radar datasets lag orders of magnitude behind vision and language. Brute-force collection will not close that gap, and existing synthesis methods (forward-only simulators, learned generators and static-scene inverse renderers) cannot fit a real capture of a moving body, leaving a sim2real gap. We present 4D Point Splatting (4DPS), a physics-based differentiable renderer that fits an explicit moving scene to a real capture. Using the synchronized camera to initialize the room and body, we represent the scene as oriented points carrying material, normal and velocity, and splat each point into range and Doppler bins. Our output is the raw complex return a real radar records, so we apply the same signal processing on the rendered data to obtain any representation for training any SOTA downstream model. We fit 235 sequences on HuPR and 100 on RT-Pose, two datasets with different radars. Our reconstructions set the state of the art, with median correlations of 0.940 and 0.830 on range-azimuth, 0.829 and 0.695 on range-Doppler, and 0.988 and 0.966 on micro-Doppler. Our renders also set the state of the art in downstream sim2real gap. On RT-Pose, a pose model trained on them reaches 21.9 cm MPJPE on real data, against 16.7 cm for real training and 127.6 cm for the RF-Genesis baseline, where both the rendered- and real-trained models learn nearly the same features. Our custom CUDA kernels fit a sequence in 5.7 minutes on HuPR and 12.9 on RT-Pose on one H100, making dataset-scale inverse rendering of mmWave radar possible for the first time. This work can enable synthetic data generation for any human-centered downstream task and model, and scene editing for data augmentation.

papers.title: Electromagnetically Consistent Monostatic ISAC Beamforming: Mutual Coupling, Active Mismatch and Tx-Rx Leakage in Compact Dipole Arrays
papers.summary: Beamforming for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is usually designed on ideal array manifolds with a norm constraint on the transmit signal. In a compact monostatic transceiver this hides three antenna effects: distorted embedded patterns, beam-dependent active mismatch at the power amplifiers, and transmit-to-receive leakage that raises the radar noise floor. We build a multiport scattering model of a shared-aperture dipole array directly from method-of-moments simulations and use it to formulate a Cramer-Rao bound minimizing ISAC beamformer with multiuser SINR constraints, per-port active reflection constraints and a leakage budget, solved as a semidefinite program with a one-dimensional budget search. Full-wave evaluation shows that coupling-unaware designs miss their SINR targets by up to 6.2 dB and drive amplifiers to an equivalent VSWR above 3.3 at small spacings. For spacings from 0.3 to 0.5 wavelengths, the proposed design meets all targets with an equivalent VSWR below 2 and lowers the root Cramer-Rao bound by 32 to 53 percent for 80 dB of self-interference cancellation and by a factor of 3.4 to 5.6 for 70 dB. An independent finite-difference time-domain model of the final layout in openEMS confirms that the leakage null and the ranking of the designs are preserved.
papers.comment: 6 pages, 9 figures, 2 tables. Submitted to IEEE ICC 2027

papers.title: Wireless Link Scheduling with Graph Signal Diffusion
papers.summary: We solve long-horizon wireless link scheduling with per-link minimum transmission constraints. Fair distribution of resources across links and time steps requires stochastic scheduling, motivating a diffusion framework. Via imitation learning, we train a diffusion model to sample scheduling decisions, conditioning generation on the network topology and constraint levels. The parameterization is achieved through a U-Graph Neural Network (U-GNN) to leverage the relationship between graphs and wireless networks for learning. Our approach achieves near-optimal performance, maximizing sum rate while distributing allocations across different links over time horizons. The U-GNN-based diffusion model generalizes to requirements and network sizes unseen during training, demonstrating the robustness of the approach.

papers.title: Spectral Convergence of Sparse Bipartite Graphs via the Line-Graphon
papers.summary: Pure point spectral convergence is generally unavailable for sparse graph sequences, where Laplacian eigenvalues may remain unstable under graph growth. This poses challenges for analyzing spectral operators underlying many graph-based learning methods, including graph neural networks. We identify a class of sparse bipartite graph sequences for which eigenvalue-level spectral convergence can be recovered. Focusing on graphs with strong degree heterogeneity, we exploit the convergence properties of their line-graph sequences. Using a spectral correspondence between bipartite graph Laplacians and line-graph adjacency operators, we transfer convergence guarantees from dense line-graphs back to the original sparse graphs. This framework yields eigenvalue-level spectral convergence for a class of deterministic sparse graph sequences. We further analyze superlinear preferential attachment trees, establishing convergence to an infinite-dimensional limit operator. Numerical experiments empirically support our spectral convergence results.

papers.title: AI-Native Task-Oriented Semantic Communications over a Relay: Benefits and Vulnerabilities
papers.summary: Semantic communication (SemCom) using a relay node is considered, where the relay assists in conveying task-relevant information from a source to a destination, with meaning defined by classification labels. A joint end-to-end design of the source encoder, relay transformation, and destination decoders is developed to optimize both semantic inference accuracy and perceptual reconstruction quality for image data. Relay-assisted schemes are shown to outperform direct transmission, with gains that become more pronounced in low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) regimes across different relaying strategies. Alongside these performance benefits, however, a key security vulnerability introduced by the relay is identified, and a Byzantine attack is formulated in which the relay injects structured, learned perturbations into its transmitted signal. The attack operates on intermediate communication representations subject to channel effects, with perturbations generated through a learned mapping applied at test time. It is shown to significantly degrade semantic inference accuracy at the destination. These results reveal a clear trade-off between SemCom gains and security risks in relay-assisted systems, motivating the need for secure relay designs that account for insider threats.

papers.title: Structured Agentic Learning for Persistent Spatial Acquisition in RDT-TAIS-Assisted Communications
papers.summary: Persistent TAIS operation can reduce repeated radio-information acquisition by reusing environmental knowledge across control intervals. This knowledge changes with radio-environment evolution and current communication task. This paper studies persistent spatial knowledge maintenance for TAIS control and formulates it as a sequential information-acquisition problem that maximizes effective communication performance while accounting for physical-acquisition overhead under an outage-reliability constraint. We develop structured agentic spatial intelligence (ASI), which realizes a communication-oriented agent that maintains persistent spatial knowledge, forms beliefs from radio and context observations, and adapts physical information acquisition through closed-loop interaction with the radio environment. By jointly exploiting radio-consistent context inference, temporal knowledge-sufficiency assessment, graph-structured regional reasoning, and predictive outage-risk feedback, structured ASI determines when additional acquisition is needed, where it is directed, and how much physical information is sufficient before stopping or escalating to full radio-environment reacquisition. Numerical results show that structured ASI improves the effective rate by 2.59% while reducing acquisition overhead by 25.0% at six structural changes per 100 control intervals, and achieves a 2.82% effective-rate gain with a 41.8% overhead reduction over a heterogeneous 400-interval mission.
papers.comment: 7 pages, 4 figures. Submitted to IEEE Conference for possible publication

papers.title: SubRoformer: Subband Time-Domain Representation for Music Source Separation
papers.summary: Music source separation extracts vocals and instruments from a mixed recording, enabling remixing, content production, and music analysis. Existing systems commonly operate on waveforms or full-band spectrograms. Waveform inputs contain many samples even in short segments, whereas a single spectrogram resolution imposes a shared time-frequency resolution trade-off across frequency ranges. We propose SubRoFormer, a Transformer-based system comprising a subband module and a residual RoFormer module. The subband module decomposes the mixture into frequency-localized, lower-rate signals for separation. It then reconstructs the target waveforms from the estimated subbands. The residual RoFormer module models temporal and cross-band relationships on temporally compressed features. It combines this context with fine-rate features through gated residual fusion to estimate source-specific complex masks. On the MUSDB18-HQ test set, training only on MUSDB18-HQ yields an average signal-to-distortion ratio (SDR) of 10.63 dB across four stems using target-specific models, achieving state-of-the-art performance among the compared systems without extra training data. With 500 additional training songs, a single model jointly separating all four stems achieves an average SDR of 11.59 dB, establishing state-of-the-art performance among the compared single-model multi-stem systems trained with extra data. Code and checkpoints are released at https://github.com/ArchiMickey/SubRoformer.
papers.comment: 13 pages, 4 figures, 5 tables. Submitted to IEEE/ACM Transactions on Audio, Speech, and Language Processing

papers.title: Geometry-Aware Channel Aging in MIMO Systems: When Is Kronecker Separability Enough?
papers.summary: This letter investigates when Kronecker-separable spatial correlation approximates the covariance of multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) channels. We propose a geometry-aware channel model in which the same propagation environment determines both the Weischelberger spatial coupling matrix and the temporal correlation coefficient. The propagation environment follows a 3GPP-inspired clustered channel model. We consider a MIMO system affected by symbol-level channel aging caused by the user equipment's mobility. We schedule both uplink and downlink pilots, thereby deriving the respective spectral efficiencies (SEs) in the presence of imperfect channel state information. Numerical results show that channel aging's magnitude is strongly geometry-dependent, with diffuse propagation inducing greater temporal decorrelation and SE degradation than concentrated scattering. The results also identify regimes where Kronecker separability can be applied and regimes where geometry-aware Weischelberger coupling is needed.
papers.comment: 5 pages, 3 figures. Submitted to IEEE Wireless Communication Letters

papers.title: Phase-Matched Design of Pinching-Antenna Elements on a 60-GHz Dielectric Rod Waveguide
papers.summary: The radiation of pinching antennas, dielectric elements placed on a dielectric waveguide, depends on the element shape. We explain it with a phase-matching, or prism-coupler, picture: the guided rod mode couples into the denser antenna plate at an angle set by the plate-mode effective index, about 31 degrees at 60 GHz, and radiates through the face it reaches first. This yields a simple sizing rule linking element height to contact length. Rectangular, isosceles and right-triangular elements of equal contact length and height are compared from 53 to 67 GHz in full-wave openEMS simulations including the waveguide-to-rod transitions. The rectangle peaks sharply at the rule, reaching 15.9 dBi. The right triangle keeps its gain within 0.7 dB and its side lobes at least 10 dB down over a two-to-one height range. At the rule, both outperform the isosceles element by 1.2 to 2.1 dB, and all remain matched.
papers.comment: 5 pages, 4 figures, 1 table. Submitted to EuCAP 2027

papers.title: Angle Estimation for Initial Access in True-Time-Delay Systems: Communication and Sensing Tradeoff
papers.summary: In joint communication & sensing (JCNS) the data signal is used to obtain parameter estimates. An example is the angle of arrival (AoA) which can be used to solve the initial access problem of beam selection. true-time delay (TTD) arrays are attractive for this purpose, as their frequency-dependent response encodes the angle information in the receive signal power spectrum. This work investigates the tradeoff between angle estimation accuracy and achievable data rate for uplink signals in a TTD array. The Fisher information (FI) for the angle is used to find the bayesian Cramer-Rao lower bound (BCRLB) under the assumption of a raised cosine distributed angle prior. Maximization of the FI under a data rate constraint is solved by waterfilling power per frequency bin dependent on sensing weights. Compared to a frequency flat signal, the optimized power allocation increases the FI \approx 4.9 dB at 5% rate loss for prior width of \pm 10°. Numerical simulations show that the derived BCRLB can be attained by a maximum likelihood (ML) estimator above an signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) threshold, confirming that the FI underlying the waveform design is attainable.

papers.title: Spatial Reuse in Multi-Cell Pinching-Antenna Systems
papers.summary: In this paper, spatial reuse in a multi-cell pinching-antenna system (PASS) is investigated, where each cell employs a dielectric waveguide with one activated pinching antenna (PA) to serve a single user. Spatial reuse refers to the simultaneous use of the same time-frequency resource block (RB) by multiple spatially separated cells. Due to inter-cell interference (ICI), simultaneous transmission by all cells on the same RB may be infeasible, and multiple RBs may be required to serve all users. The spatial-reuse capability is thus characterized by the minimum number of RBs required to satisfy all users' signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) targets under per-cell power budgets. Flexible PA placement can enhance the desired-link gain of each user and reduce the required transmit power of its serving cell, which in turn mitigates ICI and allows more cells to share the same RB. To exploit these benefits, a joint optimization problem of RB allocation, PA placement, and power control is formulated. For the two-cell case, the globally optimal PA placement is determined by minimizing the peak transmit power required by the two cells. A one-dimensional special case is further analyzed to derive analytical expressions for the average RB requirement and its scaling laws with respect to cell length under different PA-placement strategies. For the general multi-cell case, the optimal two-cell solution is exploited to construct a weighted compatibility graph, whose edge weights represent the minimum peak transmit powers required for feasible pairwise RB reuse. Based on this graph, a greedy RB allocation algorithm with minimum-weight pair initialization and element-wise PA-placement optimization is developed. Numerical results validate the analytical findings and demonstrate that PASS significantly reduces the required RBs compared with conventional fixed-antenna systems.

papers.title: From Choirs to Solos: Reducing Multi-Cell Cooperation via Pinching Antennas
papers.summary: This article investigates the potential of the pinching-antenna system (PASS) to reduce multi-cell cooperation requirements. Flexible pinching-antenna (PA) placement can enhance desired channel gains and reduce the required transmit power, which consequently alleviates inter-cell interference and the need for cooperative transmission. A two-cell PASS is considered, where the cooperation cost is quantified by the number of additional base station-user data associations. The cooperation cost is minimized subject to user signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio requirements and individual transmit-power constraints. Joint PA placement and transmission designs are developed using alternating optimization and second-order cone programming, while low-complexity zero-forcing-based alternatives are also proposed. Numerical results demonstrate that PASS substantially reduces cooperation requirements compared with the conventional fixed-antenna system. These findings highlight the potential of PASS to transform cooperative multi-cell ``\emph{choirs}'' into independent ``\emph{solos}''.

papers.title: Sparse Bayesian Sensing for Antenna Arrays with Per-Element Gain, Phase, and Position Errors
papers.summary: The sensing capabilities of 6G wireless communication systems rely on accurate models of phased-array antennas. However, hardware imperfections can introduce a mismatch between the assumed and the actual array response, leading to performance degradations. To prevent these, we propose a parametric, model-based sparse Bayesian learning (SBL) channel estimation algorithm with integrated self-calibration, which accounts for antenna-position deviations as well as gain and phase offsets. The algorithm learns channel parameters such as delay and direction-of-arrival (DoA), together with per-antenna complex weights and position deviations based on fast variational SBL with dictionary refinement. We derive a marginal-likelihood-based cost function for the antenna position update. The sensing performance is evaluated in terms of the optimal subpattern-assignment (OSPA) metric of the delay and DoA. The proposed method approaches a benchmark based on the derived hybrid Cramér--Rao lower bound (HCRLB) in the considered single-snapshot sensing scenarios. Finally, we investigate the influence of the detection threshold using synthetic and measurement data. On single-snapshot measurements, our algorithm reduces the position OSPA from about 6 m to 0.2 m for an appropriately chosen threshold.

papers.title: Reliable Bistatic Ranging With Unreliable Communication Payloads
papers.summary: This paper addresses a key challenge in bistatic integrated sensing and communications (ISAC): \textit{How to achieve reliable ranging using communication data signals that cannot be reliably recovered?} In modern communication systems, data payloads typically occupy far more time-frequency resources than pilots, offering substantially more observations to improve sensing accuracy. Exploiting them requires recovering the transmitted symbols to form sensing references. However, propagation and reflection losses can severely weaken target echoes. The sensing receiver may therefore be unable to recover data transmitted at a high rate selected for communication users. We first show that, at low signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs), using hard symbol decisions as sensing references can introduce a persistent bias in the estimated channel impulse response (CIR). This bias produces an error floor and spurious peaks in the power delay profile (PDP) that persist even after coherent accumulation over a large number of observations. To address this limitation, we develop a pilot-initialized expectation-maximization (EM) estimator that iteratively refines the CIR using posterior symbol moments. Under local regularity conditions and successful initialization, we establish that the EM method converges to the local maximum-likelihood (ML) solution for a sufficiently large number of OFDM data symbols. The converged estimator is asymptotically unbiased, where the CIR estimation mean-square error (MSE) at each delay bin decays as $O(1/M)$ by accumulating $M$ data symbols. Thus, estimation error can vanish through sufficient accumulation even while symbol recovery remains highly unreliable. Numerical results validate the proposed method, demonstrating substantially higher target detection probabilities than pilot-only and hard-decision-based bistatic ranging under the same low-SNR conditions.
papers.comment: 13 pages, 7 figures, submitted to IEEE for possible publication

papers.title: Flexible Piezoelectric Tactile Sensing System for Intelligent Object Recognition
papers.summary: Tactile sensing provides information about object properties that can improve robotic grasping and manipulation. However, accurate object recognition during the early stages of grasping remains challenging, particularly under strict real-time constraints. This study presents a flexible, distributed piezoelectric tactile sensing system for early-stage object recognition. The system was experimentally evaluated using six everyday objects and three recognition approaches: feature-based classification using support vector machines (SVMs), raw-signal classification using 1D convolutional neural networks (1D-CNNs) and convolutional recurrent neural networks (C-RNNs), and spatiotemporal heatmap classification using a 2D-CNN. The effects of sensor count and temporal window size on recognition accuracy and real-time feasibility were systematically investigated. Increasing the number of sensing elements improved recognition performance across all approaches. The best-performing method, based on spatiotemporal heatmaps and a 2D-CNN, achieved F1-scores of 0.9796, 0.9846, and 0.9903 using 16, 24, and 32 sensors, respectively. The optimal configuration, comprising 32 sensors and a 100-ms temporal window (50 samples), was deployed on an embedded edge platform, achieving an end-to-end recognition latency of approximately 101 ms from contact onset and an energy consumption of 63.8 microjoules per inference. These results demonstrate the potential of distributed piezoelectric tactile sensing for accurate, energy-efficient, and real-time object recognition during robotic grasping.
papers.journal_ref: IEEE SENSORS JOURNAL, VOL. 26, NO. 8, 15 APRIL 2026

papers.title: Fast and Convergent Alternating GPI Precoding for Self-Backhauled Satellite-Terrestrial Networks
papers.summary: In this paper, we propose a precoding framework for an integrated satellite terrestrial self-backhauled (ISTS) system, where a low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite transmits a backhaul stream to an earth station (ES), and the ES forwards its payload to the base station (BS) serving the users. We formulate a user sum spectral efficiency (SE) maximization problem subject to a self-backhaul constraint, which ensures that the user data forwarded by the BS do not exceed the data delivered to the ES. We then reformulate the resulting non-convex precoding problem into a form amenable to generalized power iteration (GPI). The GPI update is reinterpreted as projected preconditioned gradient ascent, revealing that its fixed step size may cause overshooting and non-monotonic behavior. Building on this interpretation, we first develop an alternating convergent GPI (AC-GPI), in which the fixed step is replaced by an Armijo backtracking rule, and show that a single Armijo-accepted step per block already guarantees sufficient ascent. This leads to the fast alternating convergent GPI (FAC-GPI), which performs one Armijo-accepted satellite update followed by one BS update in every round. Unlike existing backtracking-based GPI methods, whose convergence has not been established, we establish finite backtracking termination, monotone ascent, convergence to stationary points, along with a global stationarity-rate guarantee. Simulation results demonstrate stable and fast convergence as well as performance gains over existing methods.

papers.title: Uplink Enhancement for Low-Altitude UAVs via Active RISs Under Existing Cellular Infrastructure
papers.summary: The proliferation of low-altitude aerial Internet of Things applications, such as UAV-based sensing/monitoring, demands high-performance uplinks, yet terrestrial-optimized cellular networks with downtilted base station (BS) antennas form coverage holes that severely degrade aerial uplink. To address this challenge without modifying infrastructure, active reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) are introduced. Unlike existing studies with complicated active RIS optimizations, we conduct a detailed noise analysis to simplify the transmission design. By deploying one active RIS per BS sector to fully exploit multi-sector reception, we develop a joint sector maximal signal combining scheme that improves signal quality through diversity gain. Active RISs introduce amplifier noise, raising questions about their net benefit. We derive an upper bound on the power ratio between RIS-introduced noise and BS-inherent noise, revealing that the impact of RIS noise is negligible under typical operating conditions. Based on this insight, we maximize a derived lower bound of the received signal-to-noise ratio by sequentially designing the amplitude and phase of reflection coefficients with closed-form expressions. Simulation results validate the theoretical analysis on negligible RIS-introduced noise in typical systems and demonstrate that under the same array gain, a larger RIS size rather than a higher reflection gain is preferred for enhancing the low-altitude uplink transmission.
papers.comment: Minor Revision - IEEE Transactions on Communications

papers.title: Copula-Based Dependence Modeling for Resilient 6G Multi-Hop Wireless Networks
papers.summary: Reliable operation of multi-hop wireless networks requires accounting for statistical dependence among link failures caused by common propagation conditions and shared network components. This paper develops a copula-based framework for modeling node-induced dependence among link-level signal-to-noise ratios and quantifying its effect on end-to-end outage. By separating marginal fading distributions from the dependence structure, the framework captures nonlinear and tail-dependent coupling beyond conventional correlation-based models. Exact outage expressions are derived for primary-backup configurations involving edge-disjoint paths and paths with shared links. We then characterize the conditional outage probability of each candidate backup path given a primary-path failure, jointly accounting for node-induced dependence and shared-link failures. In high-reliability regimes, we derive a first-order score that decomposes conditional outage into terms associated with marginal path outage, shared links, and node-induced dependence, enabling efficient dependence-aware backup-path selection. We also establish sufficient conditions under which the first-order and exact selection rules identify the same backup path. Numerical results validate the analysis and show that copula families with the same Kendall's $τ$ can yield markedly different outage behavior because of their different tail-dependence properties. In particular, lower-tail dependence and path overlap can substantially reduce redundancy gains and reverse rankings based only on marginal outage probability.

papers.title: SVM + CFAR + OR: A Hybrid Machine-Learning-CFAR Receiver for Low-False-Alarm PRACH Preamble Detection in 5G NR and Beyond
papers.summary: The physical random access channel (PRACH) enables initial access between user equipment and the base station, making reliable preamble detection essential for cellular networks. Growing device density in 5G and beyond-5G networks, massive machine-type communication, and the shift towards machine-learning-driven radio interfaces challenge conventional analytical detectors, particularly in complex radio environments and at low signal-to-noise ratios. This article formulates preamble detection as a 64-class classification problem and introduces two model-agnostic contributions: a robust adaptive threshold implementing the constant false alarm rate (CFAR) principle in the classifier decision-score domain (MAD-CFAR), and a hybrid receiver combining a learned detector with a conventional power-delay-profile CFAR detector through a logical OR rule. The learned branch is evaluated using two models trained on the same GPU-generated dataset: a support vector machine (SVM) with principal component analysis and a lightweight one-dimensional convolutional neural network (CNN). On a held-out test set, the SVM achieves 98.58% accuracy (macro-AUC 0.9991), while the CNN reaches 99.29% accuracy (macro-AUC 1.0000) at lower inference cost and memory footprint. MAD-CFAR reduces the learned branch's false alarm rate to near zero on the noise calibration campaign. The OR hybrid retains the analytical detector's low, standard-compliant false alarm rate while extending detection capability. Across six propagation channels and 258 conformance-style tests, the SVM-based hybrid improves low-SNR sensitivity by several decibels without increasing missed detections relative to the analytical detector. Under the same false alarm constraint, the CNN is competitive in some channels but currently trails the SVM in high-delay-spread multipath conditions.

papers.title: Joint Flexible Beamforming, Resource Allocation, and Task Buffering for Movable-Antenna Enabled MEC Systems
papers.summary: The proliferation of computation-intensive applications, such as generative artificial intelligence and low-altitude economy services, demands mobile edge computing (MEC) systems that are both energy-efficient and adaptable to highly dynamic workloads. However, conventional MEC architectures rely on fixed-position antennas with limited spatial flexibility and rigid single-slot task execution models, which fail to accommodate bursty traffic and time-varying channels. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel MEC framework empowered by movable antennas (MAs) and task buffering. Unlike traditional approaches, our system enables continuous antenna repositioning to maximize array gains and decouples task generation from immediate execution via buffer queues, allowing for flexible multi-slot scheduling. We formulate a stochastic optimization problem to minimize long-term energy consumption by jointly optimizing receive beamforming, MA positions, and computing resources. Leveraging Lyapunov optimization, we transform the long-term problem into tractable per-slot subproblems and develop an efficient alternating optimization algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme significantly outperforms the benchmark schemes in terms of energy consumption, while maintaining stable task queues under unpredictable traffic conditions.

papers.title: Re-Planning Budgets under Admission Control in Grant-Free LEO Beam-Hopping Access
papers.summary: Reordering low-Earth-orbit (LEO) beam-hopping visits can reduce grant-free update delivery even when each region receives the same service time. We derive the largest limit on inter-frame position changes that meets a prescribed delivery-rate loss tolerance when every group is visited once per frame. The guarantee concerns a protected beam's spatially averaged long-run delivery rate relative to optimized periodic service under exogenous re-planning. Fixed admission can favor irregular visits, whereas admission optimized for each revisit interval makes the per-visit reward concave under sufficient conditions on transmission success. Periodic service is then optimal at a fixed mean interval. The shortest and longest allowed intervals determine the exact worst-case loss, attained by feasible alternating visit orders that respect every group's displacement limit. The resulting budget requires no estimate of the revisit-interval distribution and extends to independent stationary renewal updates. In a collision example with 40 groups and 40 resources per slot, increasing the loss tolerance from zero to 1% raises the limit from 17 to 24 positions. With independent priorities, the latter retains over 90% of the priority-weighted waiting-cost reduction achieved by unrestricted ordering. Received-power simulations under Rayleigh fading support the predicted loss.
papers.comment: 6 pages, 5 figures, 1 table, submitted to IEEE ICC 2027

papers.title: When Does Inter-BS Interference Hurt Sensing in ISAC? An Exact Fisher Information Analysis under Finite-Alphabet Interference
papers.summary: In networked integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), a base station (BS) performing sensing using its own downlink signals is subject to interference from the downlink transmissions of neighboring BSs. This paper investigates the impact of the signal constellation and waveform on the sensing performance in the presence of such inter-BS interference. For any linear receiver, we show that the mean-squared cross-ambiguity between two random ISAC signals is invariant to the modulation bases and constellations. We then derive the exact Fisher information under finite-alphabet interference with a flat-fading link, which equals the interference-free Fisher information scaled by $1-γ\,\mmse_{\C}(γ)$, where $γ$ denotes the interference-to-noise ratio (INR) and $\mmse_{\C}$ is the minimum mean-square error (MMSE) in estimating an interfering data symbol from its noise-corrupted observation at the sensing receiver. Consequently, Gaussian interference is the worst case and corresponds to the CRB loss of the matched filtering, whereas finite-alphabet interference induces a non-monotonic CRB loss that peaks at intermediate INR and vanishes at high INR. The loss is waveform-independent for the flat-fading BS-BS link, and an expectation-maximization (EM) interference-cancellation receiver approaches the theoretical bound for delay estimation.
papers.comment: 6 pages, 4 figures, submitted to IEEE possible publication

papers.title: Sharp Minimum-Rate Guarantees for Power-Based Discrete RIS Design
papers.summary: We characterise when desired-power optimisation guarantees the minimum user rate (MUR) in discrete reconfigurable intelligent surface systems with fixed precoding. For the weighted sum of desired powers, a bounded channel exists whose exact maximiser starves a user: no positive guarantee exists. For the minimum desired power, the retained fraction of the optimal MUR is at least a sharp constant set by the phase's power quality and residual interference. A semidefinite dual certifies it without enumerating phases. Minimum-power phases keep 88% of the optimum under weak reflection and about half under strong reflection; omitted interference causes most of the loss.
papers.comment: in the submission process to WCL
